source.title: Neural Network Optimization Reimagined: Decoupled Techniques for Scratch and Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Xin Ning; Qian-Kun Li; Xiao-Long Huang; Qiu-Pu Chen; F. He; Wei-Jun Li; Prayag Tiwari; Xin-Wang Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports held-out classification accuracy while testing a new layer-wise weight-decay method during training from scratch. It does not measure training-to-test gaps or test the listed versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper tests DualOpt's layer-wise weight decay on natural-label classification datasets and reports test accuracy. It does not report train error alongside test error, random-label fitting, or a measured generalization gap. Results about fine-tuning, detection, and segmentation do not test the listed claim versions and are omitted.
record.test_reason: Table II reports Adam-versus-momentum-SGD held-out accuracy for the same architectures and datasets, bearing on V4 even without training-error measurements. Adam performs better in 14 of 16 baseline comparisons; SGD performs better for Inception on CIFAR-100 and SVHN. This is a fixed-recipe comparison, with no optimizer-specific learning-rate search reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' claims about improved convergence and generalization from scratch, but omits their central fine-tuning conclusion: weight rollback and layer-wise penalties preserve upstream knowledge while improving downstream performance. Their claim of consistent from-scratch improvement is overstated: Table II reports decreases for ResNet-50 on OfficeHome with both optimizers and Inception on StanfordCars with Adam. No training-to-test gaps are reported.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces real-time layer-wise weight decay for training from scratch; the reported experiments compare the method with standard optimizers and decay strategies. It does not use the original studies' memorization, width-sweep, optimizer-comparison, batch-size, sharpness, or memorized-example procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture, optimizer, and decay strategy vary in the reported from-scratch experiments; outcomes differ across these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The extracted comparisons measure the effect of DualOpt or weight-decay placement within an optimizer, rather than the adaptive-versus-SGD contrast. Most improve accuracy, with three decreases in Table II.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-wise real-time weight decay can improve held-out image-classification accuracy, with effects depending on architecture and dataset.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The study reports held-out accuracy but no corresponding training error or train-test gap. It supplies no uncertainty estimates for the reported accuracy comparisons. The from-scratch experiments use a fixed 50-epoch duration; convergence comparisons are described in text but their figure values are not extracted here.
record.rows_left_out: Fine-tuning, detection, and segmentation results in Tables III–VIII and other analyses are outside the listed versions and do not report results on the claim's specified behaviors. Figure 3 convergence results are not extracted because they report epoch/accuracy comparisons rather than train-test gaps.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance compared with natural labels under the same recipe.
Width sweeps, interpolation thresholds, and held-out error beyond zero training error.

Optimizer-specific learning-rate and schedule tuning; relative training performance; language benchmarks; broader tuning; switching optimizers; and a controlled test of decoupled weight decay recovering an adaptive-optimizer deficit.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size effects, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with measured generalization gaps.
Memorization-based example removal versus random removal and retraining.

missing.what: Add direct baseline Adam-versus-momentum-SGD accuracy rows. In dataset order CIFAR-100, SVHN, CUB-200-2011, StanfordCars, Places-LT, IP102, OfficeHome, PACS: ResNet-50 Adam/SGD pairs are 63.47/59.93, 94.36/93.83, 28.05/15.59, 25.05/10.57, 16.33/15.38, 50.45/49.77, 52.88/43.81, 74.65/67.95; Inception pairs are 54.48/57.08, 94.48/94.98, 26.49/19.47, 26.45/14.18, 14.49/12.79, 47.87/44.30, 31.15/32.93, 75.48/62.07. Against V4, the first two Inception comparisons are observed and the other 14 are reversed. Record the shared learning rate 0.01, weight decay 0.0001, batch size 128, and 50 epochs.
missing.locator: Table II; Sections IV-D and V-A-1-a

missing.what: Add optimizer-family comparisons under the proposed decay recipe: Adam versus SGD is higher for all eight ResNet-50 datasets and seven Inception datasets; Inception CIFAR-100 instead favors SGD, 58.62 versus 56.15. Keep these separate from baseline optimizer comparisons because DualOpt changes the regularization recipe.

Table IX additionally permits Adam-versus-SGD comparisons for uniform, proposed, and inverse decay: 63.47/59.93, 64.67/60.03, and 62.61/59.67. All favor Adam. Resolve the stated ViT-B backbone versus duplicated ResNet-50 values before treating these as independent architecture evidence.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of training-error measurements does not prevent testing V4's held-out-performance comparison. The table labels the adaptive optimizer Adam, whereas implementation details specify AdamW; preserve this ambiguity. The fixed shared learning rate and short budget limit conclusions about tuned or converged optimizer performance. Existing rows correctly retain versions none for their stated within-optimizer operations; V4 verdicts use the missing direct comparisons in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error as a function of width.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under matched tuning, including the stated tuning and weight-decay qualifications.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout comparisons and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train-test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.condition: Baseline Inception on CIFAR-100 and SVHN, trained from scratch for 50 epochs with the shared reported recipe.
relationships.reason: Missing optimizer-comparison rows: Table II gives SGD versus Adam accuracy of 57.08 versus 54.48 and 94.98 versus 94.48, respectively; SGD has lower held-out error.
relationships.display_finding: Reported SGD accuracy exceeds Adam on both benchmarks under the shared recipe, but the comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Baseline ResNet-50 on all eight datasets and baseline Inception on the other six datasets, under the shared 50-epoch recipe.
relationships.reason: Missing optimizer-comparison rows: Adam has higher accuracy in all 14 comparisons, showing that adaptive methods need not perform worse under this fixed recipe; optimizer-specific tuning was not reported.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly achieved higher accuracy in all 14 comparisons under the shared recipe, but these results remain unverified and optimizer-specific tuning was unreported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
